_readme: The funds whose 13F books are reconciled against the SEC filing itself: offline in tests/edgar-reconcile.test.mjs (fixtures made by tests/fixtures/make-edgar-fixtures.mjs) and live by scripts/reconcile-edgar.mjs. Picked for the ways a 13F table goes wrong, not at random; `why` says which. `fixture: false` keeps a book that is too large to commit out of the fixtures; the live check still reads it.

funds.why: Berkshire: the same CUSIP on many lines (one per co-manager), summed into one position
Baupost: thousands written into a dollars filing, rescaled x1000
Duquesne: thousands written into a dollars filing, rescaled x1000
Himalaya: a small book, foreign issuers and ADRs
Third Point: put/call option rows next to the shares
Tiger Global: foreign issuers, filed by an agent
Soros: a few hundred rows, options and convertible notes (principal amounts)
Vision Capital: a 13F-HR/A that restates the whole table
Cisco: a 13F-HR/A that adds new holdings to the original
Luxor: an ordinary filer with option rows
